newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline Beecham 1996 profits up sharply.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline Beecham 1996 profits up sharply.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc, the big drug manufacturer, said Tuesday that profits rose 14 percent in 1996, although the strength of the British pound hurt results in the fourth quarter and year.
Pretax profit rose to 1.55 billion pounds ($2.48 billion) from 1.36 billion ($2.18 billion) in 1995. The results were at the low end of analysts' forecasts.

SmithKline Beecham said sales of its newest products again lead the way, rising 37 percent for the year. Drug sales and operating profit both rose 14 percent, while profit margins stood at 24.8 percent.
Antibiotic Augmentin and fast-growing anti-depressent Paxil/Seroxat were the biggest selling products, both helped by new formulations and uses.
Sales of Augmentin rose 4 percent to 868 million pounds ($1.39 billion) while Paxil, which competes with Eli Lilly & Co.'s Prozac, rose 42 percent to 706 million pounds ($1.13 billion).

The company said the number of people covered by its U.S. pharmacy benefit manager climbed 27 percent to 33 million, while the troubled Clinical Laboratories operations staged a modest recovery, with operating profit up 7 percent.
Sales at consumer healthcare rose 17 percent while operating profit rose 12 percent.
The company said the strong pound reduced fourth-quarter pretax profits by 35 million pounds ($56 million) and the full-year results by 29 million pounds ($46.4 million).
